issues.detail: Hebrew 'פַּחוֹת וּסְגָנִים' means 'governors and officials' (or 'deputies and prefects'), not '百夫長和王子' (centurions and princes). The Chinese rendering swaps the social/political titles for different ones.

Hebrew 'בַּחוּרֵי חֶמֶד' means 'desirable young men' or 'choice young men' (i.e., young men of beauty/desire), not '一切的少年人在恩愛中' ('all the young men in love/affection'). The Chinese adds the concept of 'in love/affection' (恩愛中) which is not in the Hebrew, and '一切的' (all) is an addition not present in the Hebrew.
